newsitem.title: INDIA: India rules on foreign funds in preference shares.
newsitem.headline: India rules on foreign funds in preference shares.

text.p: India said on Thursday that foreign investments in preference shares of Indian companies will be considered a part of share capital and will fall outside the external commercial borrowings (ECB) guidelines.

A government statement said the issue of preference shares would be permissible only as rupee denominated instruments in accordance with existing laws. This would give Indian companies greater flexibility in using preference shares as a form of financing.

The statement said the guidelines for foreign investment were would apply with immediate effect and were being issued as there had been several queries as to whether prefernce shares are to be treated as debt or equity.

The statement said proposals from companies for the issue of preference shares to foreign investors would be treated as proposals for foreign equity induction and will be processed through the regular route, and would not require separate consideration or approval from the Finance Ministry.
It stated preference shares would be included as foreign direct equity for purposes of sectoral caps on foreign equity, where such caps are prescribed, provided they carry a conversion option.
If the preference shares are structured without such conversion options, they would fall outside the foreign direct equity cap, the statement said.

It added that issue of preference shares by Indian companies would continue to conform to guidelines set by the stock market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Reserve Bank of India, and other statutory requirements.
